models.title: Capture ratio (upside over downside)
models.summary: Asymmetry of return as upside capture divided by downside capture; above 1 is convex (positive asymmetry).

relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 capture ratio with Exhibits 18/23, printed pp. 57-61 (PDF pp. 65-69): 72.8%/59.8% = 121.7%; Example 13, printed p. 65 (PDF p. 73): 118%/103% = 115%; Exhibit 23 profiles: 75%/25% = 3.0, 25%/75% = 0.3
relationship.translation_notes: Inputs are the leg ratios (decimals); output decimal (121.7% = 1.217).

assumptions: Both legs from one consistent comparison (same spans/method).
limitations: Threshold reading only (above/below 1); magnitude comparisons across managers need matched spans.

models.title: Gain required to offset a loss
models.summary: Percentage gain needed on the reduced base to recover a given percentage loss.

relationship.original_equation: g = L/(1-L): lose L of 1, hold 1-L, need L/(1-L) to recover
relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 gain-to-offset loss, Exhibit 22 discussion printed p. 61 (PDF p. 69): 50% loss needs 100% gain; Example 13 Q1 solution, printed p. 64 (PDF p. 72): lose 10% of 100 (hold 90), earn 10/90 = 11%
relationship.translation_notes: L is the loss fraction (decimal); output the required gain fraction (decimal). Source-backed derivation from the two published statements.

variables.definition: Fractional gain on the reduced base needed to recover, decimal

assumptions: Frictionless recovery (no fees, taxes, or contributions); single loss-then-gain round trip.
limitations: Total-loss (L = 1) is unrecoverable and guarded out; partial recovery paths need not follow this closed form.

models.title: Maximum drawdown
models.summary: Largest peak-to-trough fractional loss; current value relative to the running peak, floored at zero loss by guard.

relationship.original_equation: Maximum DD(m,t) = min([V(m,t) - V(m,t*)]/V(m,t*), 0), t > t*
relationship.locator: PDF: LM1 maximum drawdown with Exhibits 20-21, printed pp. 59-60 (PDF pp. 67-68): March 2020 cumulative -19.60% from December 2019 peak (+11.10%); January drawdown -0.04%; duration 7 months, 4-month recovery
relationship.translation_notes: v is the trough value (index level), vp the prior peak; output negative fraction. Inputs as index levels (1 + cumulative return). The PDF's min(...,0) floor is enforced by the v <= vp guard.

variables.definition: Portfolio value (index level) at the trough, in currency units
Prior peak portfolio value (index level), in currency units

assumptions: trough after the peak (t > t*); values as contemporaneous index levels.
limitations: Single episode statistic; duration/recovery phasing (7 months/4 months in the source) is descriptive, not part of this formula. New highs reset the peak.
